guide: This is a story about the honest side of building an app in public, so the steps below are what you can do to keep a project running when something breaks. You need a live app, an uptime monitor, and an AI coding assistant.
1. Put your app on a host such as Vercel, with Supabase or a similar service for the database, so it runs without your laptop.
1. Set up an uptime monitor such as UptimeRobot or Better Stack to email you when the site stops responding.
1. When an alert arrives, open the host's deployment and runtime logs to find the first error, not the last.
1. Paste the error, the failing file and what you changed last into Claude Code or Codex, and ask for the cause before asking for a fix.
1. Test the fix locally, deploy it, and wait for the monitor to report the site as up again.
1. Write one line in a notes page, such as Notion, with what broke and what fixed it, so the same bug is quicker next time.
1. Film or write the update as it happened, including the bug, because it shows the real process.
Watch out: Do not push a fix you have not run, as a rushed change at night can break the site again, so confirm the monitor is green before you stop.

```
You are helping me keep my web app running and fix it when it breaks. My app is <app name>, built with <framework>, hosted on <Vercel or other host>, with <Supabase or other database>. I use <UptimeRobot or Better Stack> to watch <my site URL> and it emails me when the site is down.
Do the following:
1. Read my project and list the most likely causes of downtime, such as failed builds, missing environment variables, database limits, or unhandled errors.
2. Add a simple health-check route at <path> that returns a short status message and checks the database connection.
3. Show me how to point the uptime monitor at that route.
4. When I paste an error log, explain the likely cause in plain English first, then propose the smallest fix, and tell me how to test it locally before deploying.
5. Draft a short template for a notes page with fields for date, symptom, cause and fix.
Do not change anything unrelated to the bug. Do not add new dependencies unless you explain why. Return the health-check code, the monitor setup steps and the notes template.
```
